title: Shri Gautam Motors Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
coram: Sudhir Agarwal, J. & Dr. Kaushal Jayendra Thaker, J.
disposition: Writ petition allowed; check-meter-based demand set aside
headnote: There is no provision under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 or the Electricity Act, 2003 by which an electricity bill can be raised on the basis of a check meter. The only question in the petition being whether a bill could be raised on the basis of a check meter, and the licensee's counsel having fairly admitted that there is no such provision, the demand raised on the strength of the inspection report / check meter was set aside.

holding_units.topic: No bill can be raised on the basis of a check meter
holding_units.question: Can an electricity bill/demand be raised on the basis of a check meter?
holding_units.holding: No. There is no provision under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code or the Electricity Act, 2003 permitting a bill to be raised on the basis of a check meter (as the licensee's counsel fairly admitted). The demand of Rs. 5,93,227 raised on the strength of the inspection report / check meter is set aside.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Demand of Rs. 5,93,227 based on an inspection report dated 19.2.2004 for installation HP-24; the only question was the legality of billing on a check meter.

principle_tags.application: A bill/demand cannot be raised on the basis of a check meter, there being no such provision in the Code or the Act.
